item.title: Tell About a Misread Concert Cue
item.prompt_text: At a student recital, you thought a short pause meant the tune had finished. You began to clap, then realised the player still had a final section to play. Tell someone who was not there what led to the mistake, what you noticed next, and how you now recognise the end of a piece.
item.target_grammar: Past simple and past continuous, then and when for sequence, and present simple for a habit.
item.fluency_objective: Make the pause a clear turning point. Add one direct observation before the reflection.
item.pronunciation_objective: Slow down briefly around the pause to make the story clear. Avoid copying the sound of the performance.

cues.text: Describe what made the pause look like the end.
Describe what happened after you clapped.
Say what you look for now.

item.model_opening: I went to a student recital last spring.
item.model_answer: I went to a student recital last spring. One player stopped after a loud part, and the room went quiet. I thought the tune was finished and began to clap. Then I saw that the player's hands were still in place. She looked at the music and started again. There was one short section left, and I felt a bit silly because I had stopped listening at the very moment it became quiet. Now, if I'm not sure a piece has ended, I wait and look at the player. A pause on its own doesn't tell me as much as what the player does next.
